regimen_rationale: An adjuvant bone-modifying option in an endocrine-depleted environment. Individual absolute benefit depends on recurrence risk and competing renal, dental and other harms.

mechanism.text: Zoledronic acid binds mineralised bone and inhibits osteoclast-mediated bone resorption. Clinical recurrence reductions should be attributed to trials, not inferred from this mechanism alone.

studies.population: 18,766 women with early breast cancer; 11,767 postmenopausal at entry, combining natural and artificial menopause
studies.comparison: Adjuvant bisphosphonate versus no bisphosphonate in unconfounded randomised trials
studies.follow_up: Median 5.6 woman-years; 97% enrolled in trials of 2–5 years treatment
limitations: Class-level pooled evidence, not a direct comparison of this exact NCCP five-year schedule.
No apparent benefit in the premenopausal subgroup without established endocrine depletion.
No significant heterogeneity by bisphosphonate class or schedule does not prove every regimen/duration is equivalent.
Breast cancer mortality is distinct from overall survival.

studies.population: Premenopausal stage I/II ER-positive and/or PR-positive breast cancer, fewer than 10 positive nodes; all received goserelin
studies.comparison: Tamoxifen or anastrozole, with versus without zoledronic acid 4 mg every 6 months for 3 years
limitations: Neither final-analysis effect met the trial’s predefined significance threshold; do not label the OS difference a proven survival benefit.
Three-year treatment duration differs from NCCP up to five years.
Ovarian suppression is integral; results do not support untreated premenopausal use.

clinical_position.text: ASCO-OH advises discussing adjuvant bisphosphonates with postmenopausal patients, including therapy-induced menopause, who are candidates for systemic adjuvant treatment. Benefit-risk, comorbidities, recurrence risk, cost/access and preferences inform selection. This does not replace standard anticancer treatment.

governance.text: The current NCCP source identifies this adjuvant indication as off-label in Ireland; local acknowledgement, discussion and consent are required.

important_separations: Adjuvant recurrence reduction is not the metastatic skeletal-related-event indication.
The six-monthly 4 mg source regimen is not the 5 mg yearly osteoporosis schedule.
Endocrine-related DEXA and fracture-risk management remain part of the wider plan.
A pooled relative reduction is not a personalised prediction.
